flashcard_questions.q: On what date did German troops march into the Rhineland?
Which 1925 agreements had Germany freely signed, accepting the Rhineland as demilitarised?
Which term means an area where military forces and fortifications are banned?
How many German troops entered the Rhineland in 1936?
What excuse did Hitler give for sending troops into the Rhineland?
flashcard_questions.a: He claimed France's new alliance with the Soviet Union threatened Germany.

flashcard_questions.q: What orders had Hitler given his generals if France took military action?
flashcard_questions.a: To withdraw at the first sign of French action.

flashcard_questions.q: Why could France not act alone against the remilitarisation?
flashcard_questions.a: It refused to move without British support, and Britain said no.

flashcard_questions.q: Which British politician called it 'the Germans walking into their own backyard'?
Which crisis was distracting the League when Hitler remilitarised the Rhineland?
How did Hitler's standing at home change after the Rhineland gamble?
flashcard_questions.a: It soared, because he had proved his generals wrong.

flashcard_questions.q: Which line of fortifications did Germany then build on its western border?
Which alliance between Hitler and Mussolini was signed in late 1936?

notes: 12 cards: 4 cause-effect, 3 event/agreement, 2 figure, 2 consequence, 1 term. Lean lesson, so 12 rather than 15; no card invents troop or date detail beyond the content.
